review_scope: Exhaustive archive, section and paragraph completeness checks; targeted five-language editorial comparison of evidence boundaries, central argument, conclusions and idiom. Selected source slips checked against official records. Not independent line-by-line historical certification of all twenty manuscripts.
notes: EP17 retains the distinction between FIFA's account and speculation about video assistance, conflicting accounts of the insult, incomplete voting-timing evidence, and a Swiss proceeding ending on limitation grounds rather than a merits finding.

EP18 retains the author's interpretation of Suarez's foul and its moral cost, without reclassifying the deliberate handball as legal. The passage on North Korea remains attributed reporting, not a confirmed punishment of the whole team.

EP18's five received manuscripts already correctly describe Cruyff as coach and South Africa's group-stage exit. Correct the corresponding Chinese/English source slips under the standing authorization for limited factual and wording edits.

EP18's English source also calls Fabregas an eighth Barcelona player in the 2010 final. Correct only that attribution: he was at Arsenal then. All five incoming manuscripts already avoid this attribution.

EP18's opening comparison must not imply the 2010 Germany-England match was a final. The five incoming manuscripts distinguish the earlier final correctly; make the same distinction in Chinese and English.

EP19's Chinese closing phrase conflates 2014 and South Africa; correct the date to 2010. English and all five incoming versions already have the correct chronology. Its multi-cause argument is preserved.

EP20 preserves the author's critical reading of VAR's intervention threshold. The claim that it exceeded its mandate remains authorial interpretation, not an independently adjudicated rule violation certified by this review. Preserve the distinction between allegations, guilty pleas in the wider corruption case and the hosting award itself.
Source HTML other than the explicitly recorded EP18 and EP19 phrases remains byte-for-byte protected; this batch adds no separate Traditional Chinese edition.

sources.supports: Guardiola's 1990/91 debut and Dream Team under coach Johan Cruyff.
Fabregas was at Arsenal from 2003 to 2011, not a Barcelona first-team player at the 2010 World Cup.
South Africa hosted in 2010 and became the first host eliminated in the first round.
Germany's 2010 victory over England secured a quarter-final berth; it was not the final.
